text: Synthetic paraphrase: prior thin-film spin-ice neutron work on a YSZ substrate had diffuse scattering from substrate chemical disorder that obscured key features. The new Dy2Ti2O7 film is on a Si substrate; the proposal assumes Si substrate scattering should be weak due to extinction and that there should be no higher-order scattering from the substrate.
Synthetic paraphrase: x-ray checks show a Si(111) substrate peak and a Dy2Ti2O7(222) film peak. The film is relaxed and grown as a thin film on Si with a Dy2O3 buffer layer.

Synthetic paraphrase: the experiment will use TAIPAN elastic maps in the HHL scattering plane around positions including (003), (002), and (1.5 1.5 1.5). The setup uses fixed final energy 14.87 meV, open-40-40-open collimation, vertically focused monochromator, reflection geometry because of Dy absorption, and two graphite filters to remove higher-order scattering. Measurements include 60 mK base temperature, 400 mK, and 1.2 K, with several six-hour maps.
